summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted following a fall at home after an episode of severe nausea and vomiting, in the setting of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis. He reported persistent nausea worsening since his last hospitalization, when spironolactone was increased to 300 mg daily. Workup revealed no acute intracranial injury on repeat head CT, and telemetry showed no arrhythmias. A single positive blood culture for gram-positive cocci was deemed a contaminant, and vancomycin was discontinued. Nausea was attributed to portal gastropathy and gastroparesis related to cirrhosis, with possible contribution from medication side effects. He did not vomit during hospitalization, tolerated oral liquids, and was discharged on oral ondansetron for breakthrough nausea. His liver disease remained stable with a MELD score of 11, no ascites on ultrasound, and no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence. He is currently at the top of the transplant list for his blood type and was advised on nutritional support and close follow-up with hepatology.
